modules.name: Go-Tangra Platform
modules.summary: Secure service framework, shared UI kit and development stack.

modules.name: Auth
modules.summary: Tenant identity, sessions, tokens and fine-grained authorization.

api_operations.summary: Resolve a tenant slug before sign-in (never reveals existence beyond slug validity)
Sign in with email + password (+ tenant; omitted or blank → derived from the email domain) (step 1)
Complete sign-in with a TOTP or recovery code (step 2)
Security-key request options for a pending sign-in (feature 018; the user's usable keys)
Complete sign-in with a security-key assertion (step 2; failures count toward the lockout like a wrong code)
Current user, tenant, effective roles, display name and avatar (never phone)
Mint a fresh access token from the live session
List my live sessions (paged, sorted). Without any list parameter the bare array of the previous release is returned (one release).
Password rules of the caller's tenant (shown on the change-password form)
Start TOTP enrolment (returns otpauth URI; not yet enabled)
Confirm enrolment with a code; returns recovery codes once
Disable TOTP (requires current password + code; refused when tenant requires MFA)
My second factors (authenticator app, security keys, recovery codes left, tenant requirement)
Start registering a named security key (attestation none; my keys excluded)
Finish registering a security key; the first factor returns recovery codes once
Rename one of my security keys
Remove one of my security keys after confirming a current factor (code, recovery code or key assertion)
Security-key request options that confirm a removal
Set a new password with a recovery token (single use)
Password rules for a still-valid reset token (not consumed; token in the body, never the URL; rate-limited)
Accept an invitation and set the initial password
Password rules for a still-redeemable invitation token (not consumed; token in the body, never the URL; no invitee data; rate-limited)
List users (admin); q matches email, first or last name; status=imported lists imported users; items carry avatar_url, groups, directory and invitation_id
One user of the tenant as the users list shows it (admin)
Replace a user's roles (admin; cannot grant permissions the actor lacks; last-owner protected)
Invite imported users (admin); roles and groups pass the escalation check once, before any invitation
Delete an imported user that was never activated (admin; no e-mail)
A user's second-factor methods (admin; key names and use, never key material or credential ids)
Remove a user's authenticator app, security keys and recovery codes and end their sessions (admin; not self, not a more privileged user)
Subject picker (feature 005): slug, display name, origin, module display name and retired flag of the tenant roles, any signed-in member

List roles with permissions, origin (builtin, module, custom), module and retirement (feature 019); paged and sorted. Without any list parameter the bare array of the previous release is returned (one release).
Create a custom role; permissions are qualified module:resource:action refs
Update a custom role's permissions (built-in and module roles are locked); legacy refs are accepted only if the role already holds them
Copy any role but owner into a new custom role with its current permissions (legacy grants not copied); the caller must hold every permission (feature 019)
Permission catalogue grouped by module (feature 019): qualified ref, module, module display name, grantable for the caller; retired modules omitted; legacy rows flagged

Tenant audit trail (filter by user, event_type, time), newest first. Without from/to the last 7 days are listed (to defaults to now, from to to minus 7 days). Legacy: cursor/limit alone keep the cursor shape plus total for one release; mixing both styles is validation_failed on cursor.
Registered client applications (paged, sorted). Without any list parameter the bare array of the previous release is returned (one release).
Register a client application (redirect URIs; returns secret once for confidential clients)
Create a tenant and invite its first owner
Create a time-limited, audited access grant into a tenant (SR-006)
Update own names/phone (audited by field name only); success carries X-Freya-Identity-Refresh
Replace own avatar (raw image body PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 2 MiB; re-encoded server-side)
Avatar bytes (image/jpeg, private immutable caching); 404 for other tenants, unknown ids and stale hashes
Subject picker (feature 005): public profiles of active members of the caller tenant matching name or email (<= 20; same rate limit as lookups)
Batch lookup of display name and avatar (same tenant; unknown ids omitted)
Display name and avatar of a member of the caller's tenant (rate-limited; uniform 404)
Roles a user holds with their sources (direct / groups)
Groups of the tenant with member counts and roles (admin; paged, sorted)
Delete a group; member_count must equal the current count
Members of a group, latest first (paged, sorted). Legacy: cursor alone keeps {items, next} plus total for one release; mixing both styles is validation_failed on cursor.
Add users (max 100); existing members are no-ops; escalation guard applies
Replace the group's roles; cannot grant permissions the actor lacks (owners exempt)
LDAP directory connections of the tenant (directory:manage; paged, sorted)
Create a connection; the bind password is sealed and never returned (directory:manage)
Test unsaved settings; connection_id without bind_password reuses that connection's stored password only for its own url, tls_mode and ca_pem (directory:manage)
Partial update; an omitted bind_password keeps the stored one unless url, tls_mode or ca_pem change (then validation_failed) (directory:manage)
Delete a connection; users already imported stay (directory:manage)
Test a saved connection and record last_test (directory:manage)
Preview directory entries under the connection base with their import status; nothing is written (directory:manage)
Import the chosen entries (re-fetched by uid under the base) as inactive users (directory:manage)
OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (code + PKCE S256 only); renders the console sign-in
Exchange an authorization code (+ code_verifier) for an access token

modules.name: Portal / Gateway
modules.summary: Public application edge, leased module registry and federated shell.

api_operations.summary: Identity of the caller (session or bearer) with display name and avatar
Registered modules visible to the caller with remote entries and navigation
CASL rules derived from the caller API permissions, per module
Server-sent events for registry and ability version changes (shell refetch trigger)
Per-signed-in-user SSE bus: realtime events any module publishes to the shared platform stream
Every registration with health and traffic (operators)
Federated remote assets relayed from the module (immutable caching for hashed assets; mf-manifest.json no-store)

api_operations.summary: The host's current certificates, one row per name (feature 033); no material
Certificate delivery items, paged (feature 033); reads work while delivery is disabled
One delivery item with its delivery (configuration, trigger, requested by)
Every enrolled agent (online and offline) with its version and upgrade state
Upgrade one agent, a selection or every outdated agent to the tenant target version
The tenant's automatic agent upgrade policy (defaults when none is stored)
Configure automatic agent upgrades and the target agent version
Resume automatic upgrades paused by a failed automatic upgrade
The tenant's automatic enrollment switch and keys (secrets are never returned)
Turn automatic enrollment on or off for the tenant
Create an auto-enrollment key (the secret is returned once)
Change an auto-enrollment key (name, networks, on/off, expiry, limit)
Delete an auto-enrollment key (enrolled agents keep working)
Replace the key's secret (returned once); the key id stays
Signed agent releases stored on the platform
